initial_growth.rationale: Q2 revenue +36%, DBNRR 120% and cRPO +35% support strong growth, with wide tail for enterprise slowdown and competition. Workers/AI revenue is not separated because it is not disclosed.

long_run_growth_y8.rationale: Long-run platform growth mean-reverts materially while retaining optionality from edge/security/AI traffic; AI revenue is not separately assumed.

growth_half_life_years_meta.rationale: Platform growth decays gradually as enterprise mix scales.

latent_loading_meta.rationale: Common cloud/software demand is material, with product/security execution idiosyncrasy.

terminal_margin_Y5.rationale: Y5 FCF margin spans stalled operating leverage to scaled software economics; center is an operating-leverage assumption, not a price target.

terminal_margin_Y8.rationale: Long-run margin can improve modestly with scale but remains wide because GAAP operating losses/SBC and infrastructure economics are unresolved.

half_life_years_meta.rationale: Mean reversion spans several reporting periods rather than one quarter.

shock_sigma_meta.rationale: Quarterly company-specific cash-margin uncertainty; separate from Joint Layer shared drivers.

shock_persistence_meta.rationale: Adjacent-quarter operating/cash-conversion shocks are persistent but mean-reverting.

lower_bound_meta.rationale: Plausible severe cash-margin floor for the modeled archetype; not a failure-event probability.

upper_bound_meta.rationale: Prevents temporary cash-conversion peaks from becoming permanent terminal economics.

multiple.rationale: Early positive-cash high-growth software has wide valuation uncertainty while GAAP operating profitability remains immature.
Scaled edge/security software FCF multiple with broad competition/rate/execution tails.
Maturity compression as platform growth normalizes.
Primary parity reference bridge. Mode 5.5x / 28x Y5 FCF multiple implies ~19.6% parity margin, aligned with the 20% Y5 cash-margin center; bridge use is expected to be material for thin-margin paths.

factor_correlations_meta.rationale: Positive co-movement between operating growth, cash economics and duration; idiosyncratic uncertainty remains material.

default_loading_meta.rationale: Company-specific common-factor loading chosen by business maturity and concentration; not fitted to price.

annualized_sigma_meta.rationale: Model-dependent path noise used for drawdown/path diagnostics, not terminal valuation calibration.

valuation_mean_reversion_half_life_years.rationale: Valuation dislocations mean-revert over a multi-quarter horizon.

implied_revenue_cagr_5y_meta.formula: Local deterministic preflight of Reverse Valuation v1.2.0 equation from NET_calibration_v1.0.yaml; host run_ref remains authoritative.

discount_rate_meta.rationale: Inherited from NET RV base calibration.

perturbations_meta.formula: v1.1.2 local robustness: sigma_eq=(Q84-Q16)/2; growth=base-revenue-weighted RMS segment initial_growth sigma_eq; margin=Y5 terminal margin sigma_eq; multiple=Y5 log-space sigma_eq; perturbation=0.25*sigma with absolute ceilings growth 10pp, margin 5pp, multiple 20% relative.

delta_tolerance_meta.rationale: NET: accepted v1.1.2 tolerance for |ΔP(2x,5Y)| and |ΔP(loss>30%,5Y)|.

persistence_meta.rationale: Company execution and demand/cash-conversion conditions persist across adjacent quarters.

scenario.description: US–China semiconductor technology race: Western subsidized capacity buildout, uncertain 3–5Y parity boundary, then persistent bifurcated production systems and accelerator price competition.

probability_meta.rationale: Owner explicitly requested separate probability judgment; calibration must not infer it.

meta.rationale: Scenario is conditioned on an ongoing strategic race at t0.
Western and Chinese fab buildout raises equipment cycle.
Sovereign localization accelerates.
Defense/strategic procurement rises.
AI infrastructure race sustains capex.
Power infrastructure buildout follows compute investment.
Fiscal/industrial investment pressure modestly raises rate environment.
Export controls mildly reduce cross-border addressability.
No physical Taiwan supply impairment is assumed before parity.
Compute service pricing not yet structurally reset.
Competition rises but parity has not yet been reached.
Compute and power buildout become more synchronized.
Capex race depends more on semiconductor supply capability.
Phase 1 encodes the owner thesis of strategic subsidy/capacity race before parity.
Owner thesis explicitly states a 3–5 year lag; triangular q12/q16/q20 encodes that uncertainty without selecting a point estimate.
Both systems accelerate equipment investment around parity.
Western localization response intensifies.
Strategic/defense procurement intensifies.
AI infrastructure spending remains elevated but more volatile.
Power buildout accelerates with duplicated compute systems.
Investment/fiscal intensity raises rate pressure.
Technology/export-control bifurcation reduces cross-border revenue.
Negative shift represents access friction/duplication risk, not loss of Taiwan strategic value.
Cheaper compute begins to pressure service pricing/economics.
Parity sharply increases accelerator price/performance competition.
Duplicated systems tightly couple compute and power investment.
Parity-boundary capex is supply capability dependent.
Technology capability and cross-border market access begin decoupling.
Phase 2 is deliberately volatile and temporary; it is the boundary the owner explicitly asked to study.

phases.name: Persistent Western and Chinese semiconductor systems

meta.rationale: Phase 3 starts after a four-quarter parity-boundary repricing window.
Duplicated supply chains keep equipment demand above BASE.
Strategic localization persists.
Defense/sovereign compute demand remains elevated.
Western AI buildout remains structurally above BASE.
Power infrastructure remains structurally elevated.
Rate pressure moderates but stays above BASE.
Cross-border technology revenue remains structurally impaired.
Supply-access friction remains; driver is not used as a proxy for Taiwan strategic relevance.
Cheaper non-Western chips pressure global compute service economics.
Sustained two-system competition compresses accelerator economics.
Persistent synchronized sovereign compute/power buildout.
Buildout remains supply-capability dependent.
Two production systems can improve local supply health while cross-border market access remains poor.
Persistent bifurcation, not an assumption that either bloc disappears.

official Chinese central/provincial notices where quantified
